title: Microsoft Teams: separate attendance and engagement report policy for Teams events
summary: Hold: the guidance tells administrators to check assignments with a command that changes them, and the events-setting command prints alternatives as a PowerShell pipeline. The licensing field also claims inclusion without supporting documentation, and the assertion that no administrator role is documented overlooks Microsoft's Teams Administrator permissions.

claims.claim: No Teams admin center path for the new events-report setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events policy AllowEngagementReport Teams admin center attendance engagement report events policy setting. Opened meeting-attendance-report, meeting-policies-overview and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; results document the meeting setting and the events parameter, not an events-setting UI path.

claims.claim: The events-setting call can use '-AllowEngagementReport Enabled | Disabled | ForceEnabled | ForceDisabled' as printed.
claims.quote:
[-AllowEngagementReport <String>]
Controls whether attendance and engagement reports are allowed for events.
Possible values are:
claims.fix: Print one value in the call, for example 'Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport ForceDisabled', and label it as the example that blocks reports. List Enabled, Disabled, ForceEnabled and ForceDisabled with their meanings in the note. The current pipes invoke additional commands rather than select a parameter value; the cmdlet and both parameter names themselves are documented.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsEventsPolicy can be used to check which events policy a user currently holds.
claims.quote: Assigns Teams Events policy to a user, group of users, or the entire tenant.
claims.fix: Replace 'or Grant-CsTeamsEventsPolicy' with 'or Get-CsUserPolicyAssignment -Identity <user>'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/get-csuserpolicyassignment?view=teams-ps, which returns effective assignments and explains that a missing effective policy entry means the tenant or system global default. Retain Grant only for assigning a policy, not inspecting one.

claims.quote: Assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment, or to a group that the users are members of.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/policy-assignment-overview to sources and link the existing mention of the policy assignment overview directly to it.
